title: Client Services Desk Basis — One Plan per Unit and Separate Plans per Building on the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans
content:
The desk basis for holding more than one of the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans is the following clause:

> A building owner may hold several warranty plans, but a unit is covered by one plan at a time. A plan is not quoted for a unit that already stands on a plan in quoted, active, pending renewal or suspended status; that plan is amended or allowed to run out first. Units at different buildings are written on separate plans, and one plan never carries more units than the tier's maximum. Claim allowances and caps are held per plan, so two plans of one owner never lend each other cover, and a unit moved between plans starts a fresh waiting period.

No ceiling is set on the number of plans one owner holds.

## The clause broken into its conditions

| Condition | Judgement |
|---|---|
| The owner already holds one or more warranty plans | The owner may hold several; the number of plans is not itself a bar. |
| A unit on the requested quote already stands on a plan whose status is quoted, active, pending renewal or suspended | No plan is quoted for that unit; the plan it stands on is amended, or is allowed to run out, first. |
| Units at two different buildings are to be covered | They are written on separate plans, one per building. |
| The units asked for exceed the tier's maximum units on one plan | One plan never carries more than that maximum. |
| One of the owner's plans has allowance or cap left and another has none | Allowance and caps are held per plan; the plans never lend each other cover. |
| A unit is moved from one plan to another | It starts a fresh waiting period on the plan it moves to. |

## What decides whether a unit already stands on a plan

The plan records at the building, and the status those records show, decide it. The record's status is read at the moment the quote is considered, and it is the office record of the plan — not a statement about the plan — that is consulted; the correlation is by the building the unit is at.

### Plan status and whether it stands in the way of a new quote for the same unit

| Status of the plan the unit stands on | A new plan may be quoted for that unit |
|---|---|
| Quoted | No |
| Active | No |
| Pending renewal | No |
| Suspended | No |
| Expired | Not barred by this clause |
| Cancelled | Not barred by this clause |
| Declined | Not barred by this clause |

The four barring statuses are the ones the clause names; the three remaining lifecycle statuses are not among them.

## Hypothetical cases

- An owner holds an active Parts Protection Plan on a rooftop unit at one building and asks for a Compressor Coverage Plan on the same unit. The unit stands on a plan in active status, so the Compressor Coverage Plan is not quoted for it; the existing plan is amended or allowed to run out first.
- An owner's plan on a unit expired last year and has not been renewed. The unit stands on no plan in a barring status, and a fresh plan may be quoted for it.
- An owner holds a plan at each of two buildings. A claim on one building's plan draws only on that plan's own allowance; the other plan's allowance is never drawn on for it.
- A unit is moved from one plan to another mid-term. The waiting period on the receiving plan runs afresh for that unit from the move.
